memory_line: Blood thinner plus a fall: no small bumps.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 1:30 AM. He's 78, on apixaban (a blood thinner) for a past clot in his leg.
• Unwitnessed fall on the way to the bathroom
• Small bump on his forehead. "I'm fine."

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ "Just a bump." Not reported
2️⃣ No neuro checks
3️⃣ Called his new sleepiness "just tired"
➡️ 4:20 AM: hard to wake, one pupil bigger, vomiting. Rapid response.

🩸 Apixaban (NO SMALL BUMPS)
• A DOAC (direct oral anticoagulant): blocks clotting factor Xa
• No INR (international normalized ratio) to watch, but bleeding risk is real
• A brain bleed can grow slowly. He can look fine for hours

✅ The right move
• Any fall with a head strike on a blood thinner: report now
• Neuro checks per your fall protocol: alertness, pupils, speech, strength
• Head CT (computed tomography) as ordered, even if he feels fine
• Red flags: worse headache, vomiting, sleepiness, confusion, unequal pupils
• Bleeding confirmed? Reversal as ordered, usually a PCC (prothrombin complex concentrate)

🧠 Blood thinner plus a fall: no small bumps.

rn_checks: Apixaban: direct factor Xa inhibitor; no routine INR monitoring
Head injury on an anticoagulant: NICE NG232 says consider a CT head within 8 hours even without other risk factors; the Reel says "head CT as ordered"

Reversal for life-threatening bleeding on apixaban: 4-factor PCC, as ordered. Andexanet alfa was withdrawn from the US market in Dec 2025 (FDA safety communication); still authorized in Canada as Ondexxya, so it is not named
Story: fall 1:30, deterioration 4:20 with a dilated pupil, vomiting, BP 186/94, heart rate 52. Realistic? (Cushing's triad not named: Beck's vs Cushing's posted Nov 5)
Close to the Nov 16 warfarin bleed Reel (heparin vs warfarin), but apixaban is a different drug. OK under the 30-day rule?
Atrial fibrillation not named (posted within 30 days): reason given is a past leg clot
